evidence.claim: Campbellsville’s public square cost the county one dollar.
evidence.quote: The city agreed to sell the public square to the county for one dollar so that a courthouse could be built.

evidence.claim: When Taylor County separated from Green County in 1848, the legislature made Campbellsville its seat, and the city sold the square for a courthouse.
evidence.quote: Campbellsville was designated by the state legislature as the county seat in 1848 after Taylor County was separated from Green County.

evidence.claim: Confederate cavalry burned that first courthouse in 1864 because Union troops were using it as barracks.
evidence.quote: The city's first courthouse was burned by Confederate cavalry in 1864 because the Union Army was using it for barracks.

evidence.claim: A second courthouse followed on the same site after the war.
evidence.quote: After the war, a second courthouse was built on the same site.

evidence.claim: The historic commercial district includes several blocks of Main Street, while a fourth courthouse, the Justice Center, was built on Main Street in 2008.

evidence.claim: The town had prospered as a river port in the late nineteenth century, when water transport offered the most feasible way to move bulk goods.
evidence.quote: Burkesville was a fairly busy river port whose heyday came during the latter part of the nineteenth century, when water transportation was the most feasible way to move large quantities of goods.

evidence.claim: Wolf Creek Dam, built upstream without a lock, curtailed commercial navigation while controlling floods.
evidence.quote: The dam controlled flooding that had plagued the town from its beginning, but was the last nail in the coffin of commercial navigation.

evidence.claim: River Street still runs directly toward the Cumberland River and the town’s public boat ramp.
evidence.quote: River Street runs straight toward the Cumberland River and provides access to the town's only public boat ramp

evidence.claim: built upstream without a lock

evidence.claim: Albany grew from a tavern established by Benjamin Dowell in the early nineteenth century.
evidence.quote: The community of Albany grew up around a tavern established by Benjamin Dowell in the early 19th century.

evidence.claim: Residents chose the location for their county seat in 1837.
evidence.quote: In 1837, residents voted to make the location the seat of county government.

evidence.claim: The generally accepted namesake is Albany, New York, but a local legend credits tavern patrons calling for Benny during the vote.
evidence.quote: It is generally accepted that the town, formally incorporated on January 27, 1838, was named after Albany, New York, but a local legend holds that, during the vote to determine the location of the county seat, patrons of Dowell's tavern shouted "All for Benny!"

evidence.claim: The Albany-Clinton County Chamber of Commerce carries that story into its annual “All for Benny” dinner on the courthouse square.
evidence.quote: The Albany-Clinton County Chamber of Commerce has an annual dinner on the courthouse square called "All for Benny."

evidence.claim: The town lies at the western edge of the Cumberland Plateau, with Albany Rock rising to the northeast.
evidence.quote: at the foot of the western edge of the Cumberland Plateau. Albany Rock, the peak of a western spur of the plateau, rises northeast of the city

evidence.claim: Cumberland Falls drops 68 feet inside the Daniel Boone National Forest.
evidence.quote: contained entirely within the Daniel Boone National Forest. The park encompasses 1,657 acres (671 ha) and is named for its major feature, 68-foot-tall (21 m) Cumberland Falls.

evidence.claim: In 1927, discussion of a hydroelectric plant above the falls prompted T. Coleman du Pont to offer to buy the falls and surrounding land for a state park.
evidence.quote: After the discussion of building a hydroelectric power plant above the falls in 1927, Kentucky native T. Coleman du Pont offered to buy the falls and surrounding acreage in order to create a state park.

evidence.claim: He died before completing the purchase; his wife bought the falls and 593 surrounding acres in 1930 after the legislature approved the park.
evidence.quote: Although he died before he could purchase the land, his wife purchased the falls and the 593 acres (240 ha) surrounding it for $400,000 on March 10, 1930, after the Kentucky General Assembly (legislature) approved the creation of the state park.

evidence.claim: The park was dedicated in 1931.
evidence.quote: Cumberland Falls was dedicated as a state park at 1:30 p.m. on August 21, 1931.

evidence.claim: On full-moon nights, a moonbow can frequently be seen at the falls.
evidence.quote: a moonbow can frequently be seen on nights with a full moon.

evidence.claim: Congress named the impoundment Lake Cumberland in 1952, adopting a name promoted by area business interests.
evidence.quote: Congress named the impoundment Lake Cumberland in 1952, adopting the name promoted by business interests in the area.

evidence.claim: At Campbellsville, access is by two-lane roads.
evidence.quote: Campbellsville is accessible by two-lane roadways.

evidence.claim: Andrew Campbell, who owned a gristmill and tavern, began selling town lots in 1814.
evidence.quote: Campbell owned a gristmill and a tavern and began selling lots in Campbellsville in 1814.

evidence.claim: Keeping larger river craft moving this far upstream had required diligent dredging of the riverbed to maintain a navigable channel.
evidence.quote: The rise of larger craft, such as the riverboat, required diligent dredging of the riverbed to keep it navigable so far upstream.

evidence.claim: Formal incorporation followed on January 27, 1838, the year after the vote.
evidence.quote: the town, formally incorporated on January 27, 1838,

evidence.quote: The section of the Cumberland River that includes the falls was designated a Kentucky Wild River by the Kentucky General Assembly through the Office of Kentucky Nature Preserves' Wild Rivers System. The forest in the park is also a dedicated State Nature Preserve.
